items.name: monad
items.statement_summary: A monad ⟨T,η,μ⟩ in a category X is an endofunctor T:X→X together with natural transformations η:Id_X⇒T (unit) and μ:T²⇒T (multiplication) satisfying the associative law μ∘Tμ = μ∘μT : T³⇒T and the two unit laws μ∘ηT = 1_T = μ∘Tη : T⇒T.

items.name: a monad is a monoid in the endofunctor category
items.statement_summary: A monad in X is exactly a monoid object in the strict monoidal category of endofunctors (End(X), ∘, Id_X): functor composition replaces the tensor ×, the identity endofunctor replaces the unit object, η is the monoid unit and μ the monoid multiplication; the monad laws are the monoid associativity and unit laws.

items.name: the monad defined by an adjunction
items.statement_summary: Every adjunction ⟨F,G,η,ε⟩:X⇀A induces a monad in X on the endofunctor T=GF, with unit the adjunction unit η and multiplication μ=GεF:GFGF⇒GF; associativity follows from naturality of ε (the interchange law) and the unit laws from the triangle identities. This monad is called the monad defined by the adjunction.

items.name: comonad
items.statement_summary: Dually, a comonad in a category A is a functor L:A→A with natural transformations ε:L⇒Id_A (counit) and δ:L⇒L² (comultiplication) making the coassociativity square Lδ∘δ = δL∘δ and the counit laws εL∘δ = 1_L = Lε∘δ commute.

items.name: the comonad defined by an adjunction
items.statement_summary: Every adjunction ⟨F,G,η,ε⟩:X⇀A defines a comonad ⟨FG, ε, FηG⟩ in A, dual to the monad GF it induces in X.

items.name: monads in a preorder are (in a poset) closure operations
items.statement_summary: In a preorder P viewed as a category, an endofunctor is just a monotone map T:P→P, and it carries monad structure η,μ exactly when x≤Tx and T(Tx)≤Tx for all x (all monad diagrams then commute automatically). If P is a partial order this forces T(Tx)=Tx, so a monad in P is precisely a closure operation t: a monotone map with x≤tx and t(tx)=tx.

items.name: T-algebra (Eilenberg–Moore algebra) and its morphisms
items.statement_summary: For a monad T=⟨T,η,μ⟩ in X, a T-algebra ⟨x,h⟩ is an object x∈X (the underlying object) with an arrow h:Tx→x (the structure map) satisfying the associative law h∘Th = h∘μ_x : T²x→x and the unit law h∘η_x = 1_x. A morphism f:⟨x,h⟩→⟨x',h'⟩ of T-algebras is an arrow f:x→x' of X with f∘h = h'∘Tf.

items.name: Every monad is defined by its T-algebras (Eilenberg–Moore)
items.statement_summary: For a monad ⟨T,η,μ⟩ in X, the T-algebras and their morphisms form a category X^T, and there is an adjunction ⟨F^T,G^T;η^T,ε^T⟩:X⇀X^T whose right adjoint G^T:X^T→X forgets the structure map (⟨x,h⟩↦x, f↦f) and whose left adjoint F^T sends x to the free algebra ⟨Tx,μ_x⟩ (f↦Tf); the unit is η^T=η and the counit is ε^T_{⟨x,h⟩}=h. The monad induced in X by this adjunction is the original ⟨T,η,μ⟩.

items.name: algebras for a closure operation are the closed elements
items.statement_summary: For a closure operation T on a preorder P (regarded as a monad), a T-algebra is an element x with structure map Tx≤x; since always x≤Tx this gives x≅Tx, and when P is a partial order x=Tx — so the T-algebras are exactly the closed (fixed) elements of P.

items.name: algebras for the monad G×(−) are G-actions
items.statement_summary: For a group G the endofunctor TX=G×X on Set, with unit x↦⟨e,x⟩ and multiplication ⟨g₁,⟨g₂,x⟩⟩↦⟨g₁g₂,x⟩, is a monad; a T-algebra ⟨X,h⟩ is a set with h:G×X→X satisfying h(g₁g₂,x)=h(g₁,h(g₂,x)) and h(e,x)=x — i.e. exactly a left G-action (G-set).

items.name: algebras for the monad R⊗(−) on Ab are left R-modules
items.statement_summary: For a ring R the endofunctor TA=R⊗A on Ab, with unit a↦1⊗a and multiplication r₁⊗(r₂⊗a)↦r₁r₂⊗a, is a monad whose T-algebras are exactly the left R-modules.

items.name: the power-set monad and complete semilattices (Manes)
items.statement_summary: Let 𝒫 be the covariant power-set functor on Set with η_X(x)={x} and μ_X = union of a set of subsets. Prove: (a) ⟨𝒫,η,μ⟩ is a monad; (b) each 𝒫-algebra ⟨X,h⟩ is a complete semilattice under x≤y iff h{x,y}=y, with sup S = h(S); (c) conversely every small complete semilattice is a 𝒫-algebra; (d) the category of 𝒫-algebras is the category of small complete semilattices and sup-preserving maps.

items.name: the algebra forgetful functor creates limits
items.statement_summary: Show that the forgetful functor G^T:X^T→X of the Eilenberg–Moore category creates limits.

items.name: morphisms of monads and the induced functor between algebra categories
items.statement_summary: (a) For monads ⟨T,η,μ⟩ and ⟨T',η',μ'⟩ on X, define a monad morphism θ:T⇒T' as a suitable natural transformation (compatible with units and multiplications) and construct the category of all monads on X. (b) From θ construct a functor θ*:X^{T'}→X^T with G^T∘θ*=G^{T'} together with a natural transformation F^{T'}⇒θ*∘F^T.

items.name: Comparison of adjunctions with algebras (the comparison functor K)
items.statement_summary: For an adjunction ⟨F,G,η,ε⟩:X⇀A defining the monad T=⟨GF,η,GεF⟩ in X, there is a unique functor K:A→X^T with G^T∘K=G and K∘F=F^T; explicitly K a = ⟨Ga, Gε_a⟩ and K f = G f. (When K is an isomorphism G is monadic.)

items.name: monadic (tripleable) functor
items.statement_summary: A right adjoint G is called monadic (tripleable) when the comparison functor K:A→X^T is an isomorphism of categories; some authors (Barr–Wells) require only that K be an equivalence of categories.

items.name: discrete-space adjunction yields the identity monad; Top is not monadic over Set here
items.statement_summary: The forgetful G:Top→Set has left adjoint D (discrete topology) with unit η_X=id; the induced monad on Set is the identity monad I=⟨Id,1,1⟩, whose algebras are just sets, so the comparison functor Top→Top^I=Set is G itself — neither an isomorphism nor an equivalence, an explicit non-monadic adjunction.

items.name: the free semigroup functor and adjunction Set⇀Smgrp
items.statement_summary: The free semigroup WX on a set X consists of all nonempty words ⟨x₁⟩…⟨x_n⟩ (n≥1) in letters of X multiplied by juxtaposition, giving a semigroup FX=⟨WX,v⟩ with WX=⨆_{n≥1}X^n; the map η_X:X→GFX, x↦⟨x⟩ is universal from X to the forgetful G:Smgrp→Set, so F is left adjoint to G and η defines an adjunction ⟨F,G,η,ε⟩:Set⇀Smgrp; the counit ε_S(⟨s₁⟩…⟨s_n⟩)=s₁…s_n (product in S) removes the pointy brackets.

items.name: the word monad W on Set
items.statement_summary: The monad on Set induced by the free-semigroup adjunction Set⇀Smgrp is W=⟨W,η,μ⟩ with WX=⨆_{n≥1}X^n, unit η_X(x)=⟨x⟩ (the one-letter word), and multiplication μ_X that erases the outer brackets of a word-of-words, sending ⟨⟨x₁₁⟩…⟨x_{1n₁}⟩…⟨x_{k1}⟩…⟨x_{kn_k}⟩⟩ to the concatenated word ⟨x₁₁⟩…⟨x_{kn_k}⟩.

items.name: algebras for the word monad W
items.statement_summary: A W-algebra is a set S equipped with one n-ary operation v_n:S^n→S for each n≥1 such that v₁=1_S and, for every k≥1 and positive n₁,…,n_k, v_k∘(v_{n₁}×…×v_{n_k}) = v_{n₁+…+n_k} : S^{n₁+…+n_k}→S; a morphism of W-algebras is a function f:S→S' commuting with every operation, f∘v_n = v'_n∘f^n.

items.name: W-algebras are semigroups with iterated multiplications
items.statement_summary: A system ⟨S,v₁,v₂,…⟩ is a W-algebra iff v₁=1_S, v₂:S×S→S is an associative binary operation, and v_{n+1}=v_n∘(v₂×1):S^{n+1}→S for all n≥2 (so every v_n is the n-fold product determined by v₂).

items.name: Smgrp is monadic over Set (the comparison functor is an isomorphism)
items.statement_summary: The comparison functor K:Smgrp→Set^W, sending a semigroup ⟨S,v⟩ to ⟨S,1,v,…,v_n,…⟩ with each v_n the iterated product, is an isomorphism of categories — so the forgetful G:Smgrp→Set is monadic; K merely re-expresses one associative binary operation as the family of all its iterated operations.

items.name: the monoid monad W0 and its algebras
items.statement_summary: For the monad W₀ on Set defined by the forgetful Mon→Set, show a W₀-algebra is a set M with a string v₀,v₁,… of n-ary operations where v₀:*→M is the monoid unit and v_n is the n-fold product.

items.name: the free R-module monad on Set and its algebras
items.statement_summary: For a ring R with identity the forgetful R-Mod→Set has a left adjoint, giving a monad ⟨T_R,η,μ⟩ on Set. (a) Describe it: T_R X = finitely-supported functions f:X→R; for t:X→Y, [(T_R t)f]_y = Σ f_x over x with tx=y; η_X x is the indicator at x; μ_X k assigns x↦Σ_f k_f f_x. (b) Verify directly it is a monad. (c) Show its algebras are the usual R-modules, presented via all linear-combination operations (the structure map sends f to the linear combination with coefficients f_x).

items.name: the polynomial-ring monad from CRng
items.statement_summary: Give a complete description of the adjunction defined by the forgetful CRng→Set, in which TX is the ring of all polynomials with integer coefficients in indeterminates x∈X.

items.name: the tensor-algebra monad on Ab and rings as its algebras
items.statement_summary: For the adjunction ⟨F,G,φ⟩:Ab⇀Rng whose G forgets ring multiplication, the induced monad T on Ab. (a) Describe T directly as for W but with X^n replaced by the n-fold tensor power and ⨆ by the direct sum of abelian groups. (b) Describe its T-algebras and show the comparison functor from rings to T-algebras is an isomorphism.

items.name: restricting an adjunction to a full subcategory of free objects
items.statement_summary: Given ⟨F,G,φ⟩:X⇀A, any full subcategory B⊆A containing every Fx yields an adjunction ⟨F_B,G_B,φ_B⟩:X⇀B (F with codomain restricted, G with domain restricted) via the same natural bijection hom_B(F_B x,b)≅hom_X(x,G_B b); this second adjunction defines the same monad in X, showing one monad arises from many adjunctions — the smallest being B = the full subcategory FX of free objects.

items.name: the Kleisli category of a monad
items.statement_summary: For a monad ⟨T,η,μ⟩ in X, the Kleisli category X_T has an object x_T per x∈X and an arrow f♭:x_T→y_T per X-arrow f:x→Ty, with composition g♭∘f♭ = (μ_z∘Tg∘f)♭. Functors F_T:X→X_T (k:x→y ↦ (η_y∘k)♭) and G_T:X_T→X (f♭ ↦ μ_y∘Tf, so G_T F_T x = Tx) form an adjunction ⟨F_T,G_T,φ_T⟩:X⇀X_T (via f♭↦f) whose induced monad in X is the original ⟨T,η,μ⟩; the unit is η and the counit is (ε_T)_{y_T}=(1_{Ty})♭.

items.name: comparison theorem for the Kleisli construction
items.statement_summary: For an adjunction ⟨F,G,ε⟩:X⇀A defining the monad T=⟨GF,η,GεF⟩, there is a unique functor L:X_T→A with G∘L = G_T and L∘F_T = F.

items.name: Kleisli initial and Eilenberg–Moore terminal among adjunctions for a monad
items.statement_summary: For a fixed monad ⟨T,η,μ⟩ in X, the category whose objects are the adjunctions ⟨F,G,ε⟩:X⇀A that define this monad and whose arrows are maps of adjunctions which are the identity on X has the Kleisli construction X_T as initial object and the Eilenberg–Moore construction ⟨F^T,G^T,η,ε^T⟩:X⇀X^T as terminal object, connected by the comparison functors X_T →(L) A →(K) X^T.

items.name: the Kleisli comparison functor and its image
items.statement_summary: Construct the Kleisli comparison functor L, prove its uniqueness, and show that the image of X_T under L is the full subcategory FX of A on the objects Fx, x∈X.

items.name: Kleisli category is equivalent to the free objects
items.statement_summary: Show that the restriction of L gives an equivalence of categories X_T→FX.

items.name: the equivalence X_T→FX need not be an isomorphism
items.statement_summary: Construct an adjunction whose F is not a bijection on objects, and deduce that the equivalence X_T→FX of Exercise 2 need not be an isomorphism (suggestion: S↦T(S)= the one-point set defines a monad on Set).

items.name: existence of the category of all adjunctions defining a monad
items.statement_summary: In the summary comparison Theorem 3, ask whether the category of all such adjunctions really exists (a size/foundational question).

items.name: composing with an identity-monad adjunction preserves the induced monad
items.statement_summary: If ⟨F,G,η,ε⟩:X⇀B defines the monad ⟨T,η,μ⟩ in X, while a second adjunction ⟨L,R,η',ε'⟩:B⇀A defines the identity monad in B (RL=I_B, η'=1, Rε'L=1), prove that the composite adjunction X⇀A defines in X the same monad ⟨T,η,μ⟩.

items.name: fork
items.statement_summary: A fork in a category C on a parallel pair d0,d1 : a => b is an arrow e : b -> c with e.d0 = e.d1; equivalently a cone from the diagram a => b to a vertex c.

items.name: absolute coequalizer
items.statement_summary: An arrow e is an absolute coequalizer of d0,d1 in C if for every functor T : C -> X (to any X) the image fork Ta => Tb -> Tc has Te a coequalizer of T.d0, T.d1; in particular an absolute coequalizer is itself a coequalizer. Absolute colimits/limits are defined analogously (Pare 1971a).

items.name: split fork
items.statement_summary: A split fork is a fork (d0,d1,e) equipped with arrows t : b -> a and s : c -> b satisfying e.d0 = e.d1, e.s = 1_c, d0.t = 1_b, and d1.t = s.e; s and t 'split' the fork. Then e is a split epi with right inverse s. Equivalently the data is a pair of commutative squares (in the arrow category C^2) whose two horizontal composites are identities.

items.name: in a split fork e is the coequalizer
items.statement_summary: In every split fork, e is the coequalizer of d0 and d1. (Any f : b -> d with f.d0 = f.d1 factors as f = (f.s).e, and any factorization f = k.e forces k = f.s, giving uniqueness.)

items.name: split coequalizer
items.statement_summary: A split coequalizer of d0,d1 is the arrow e of some split fork on d0,d1.

items.name: in a split fork e is an absolute coequalizer
items.statement_summary: In every split fork, e is an absolute coequalizer of d0 and d1: since the split-fork equations involve only composites and identities they are preserved by any functor, so the image fork is again a split fork, hence a coequalizer.

items.name: split fork in Cat (arrow category over terminal)
items.statement_summary: In Cat, for any category C, the diagram C^2 => C -> 1 is a fork: C^2 is the arrow category, d0 and d1 are the domain and codomain functors, and e is the unique functor C -> 1. If C has a terminal object a0 the fork is split, by s sending 1's object to a0 and t sending each object c to the unique arrow c -> a0.

items.name: quotient group as a coequalizer in Grp
items.statement_summary: For a normal subgroup N <| G, form the semidirect product G x0 N (elements (x,n) with x in G, n in N; multiplication (x,n)(y,m) = (xy, (y^-1 n y) m)). Then G x0 N => G -> G/N is a fork, with d0(x,n)=x, d1(x,n)=xn, and p the quotient projection; p is the coequalizer of d0,d1 in Grp. This fork is not split in Grp in general, but applying the forgetful U : Grp -> Set makes it split (s a coset-representative section, t x = (x, x^-1 (s p x))). Thus every quotient group is a coequalizer in Grp.

items.name: quotient ring as a coequalizer in Rng
items.statement_summary: In Rng, exhibit every quotient R/A of a ring R by an ideal A as a coequalizer, and show the resulting fork becomes split after applying the forgetful functor to Set.

items.name: contractible (Beck) pair
items.statement_summary: Contractible (Beck) parallel pair: a pair d0,d1:a->b is contractible if there is t:b->a with d0.t = 1_b and d1.t.d0 = d1.t.d1. (a) the pair of any split fork is contractible; (b) a contractible pair whose coequalizer exists has that coequalizer split. [equation recovered from PDF 159; earlier scan misread 'd1.t = d0.d1' was non-composable.]

items.name: Beck's theorem characterizing algebras
items.statement_summary: Let <F,G,eta,eps> : X -> A be an adjunction inducing the monad <T,eta,mu> on X, let X^T be its category of T-algebras and <F^T,G^T,eta^T,eps^T> the Eilenberg-Moore adjunction. Then the following are equivalent: (i) the unique comparison functor K : A -> X^T is an isomorphism; (ii) G : A -> X creates coequalizers for exactly those parallel pairs f,g in A for which <Gf,Gg> has an absolute coequalizer in X; (iii) the same with 'absolute coequalizer' replaced by 'split coequalizer'. (Precise monadicity/tripleability; 'creates coequalizers' as in Sec V.1.)

items.name: canonical presentation of an object
items.statement_summary: For each object a in A the adjunction <F,G,eps,eta> yields a fork FGFGa => FGa -> a (arrows eps_{FGa} and FG(eps_a), coequalized by eps_a), called the canonical presentation of a (for A = Grp it is the free-group presentation). Applying G gives a split fork, the canonical presentation of the T-algebra <Ga, G eps_a>.

items.name: comparison of two adjunctions defining the same monad
items.statement_summary: Given adjunctions <F,G,eta,eps> : X -> A and <F',G',eta',eps'> : X -> A' inducing the same monad T on X, a comparison (of F' to F) is a functor M : A' -> A with M.F' = F and G.M = G'. Such an M is a morphism of adjunctions and hence satisfies M.eps' = eps.M.

items.name: existence/uniqueness of the comparison under creation of coequalizers
items.statement_summary: If G satisfies hypothesis (iii) of Beck's theorem (creates coequalizers of pairs with a split coequalizer under G), then for any other adjunction <F',G',eta',eps'> defining the same monad there is a unique comparison M : A' -> A. Applied to the Eilenberg-Moore adjunction (which satisfies (iii)) this reproves the comparison theorem of Sec 3; it also supplies the M used in proving (iii)=>(i) of Beck's theorem.

items.name: reflects colimits (coequalizers, isomorphisms)
items.statement_summary: A functor G : A -> X reflects colimits of T : J -> A when every cone lambda : T -> a in A whose image G.lambda : GT -> Ga is a colimiting cone in X is already colimiting in A. Specializations: G reflects coequalizers (a fork in A that G sends to a coequalizer is already a coequalizer), and G reflects isomorphisms (for every arrow t of A, Gt an isomorphism implies t an isomorphism).

items.name: CTT, VTT, PTT tripleability properties of a functor
items.statement_summary: For G : A -> X let C_G (resp. S_G) be the set of parallel pairs <f,g> in A for which <Gf,Gg> has a coequalizer (resp. a split coequalizer) in X. G is CTT (crude tripleable) if G has a left adjoint, preserves and reflects coequalizers of all pairs in C_G, and A has coequalizers of all pairs in C_G. G is VTT (vulgar tripleable) if G has a left adjoint, reflects coequalizers of all pairs in S_G, and A has split coequalizers of all pairs in S_G. G is PTT (precise tripleable) if G has a left adjoint, preserves and reflects coequalizers of all pairs in S_G, and A has coequalizers of all pairs in S_G. Both CTT and VTT imply PTT. (More authoritative CTT/VTT definitions are in Barr-Wells 1985.)

items.name: creates implies reflects coequalizers
items.statement_summary: If G creates coequalizers, prove that G also reflects coequalizers. ('coequalizers' throughout means coequalizers of parallel pairs.)

items.name: Weak Tripleability Theorem (Beck's thesis)
items.statement_summary: Given the adjunction (1) and comparison functor K, give a direct proof that: (a) if A has all coequalizers then K has a left adjoint L; (b) if in addition G preserves all coequalizers then the unit is an isomorphism I ~= K.L; (c) if in addition G reflects all coequalizers then the counit is an isomorphism L.K ~= I.

items.name: preserves + reflects-isos gives reflects coequalizers
items.statement_summary: (Alternative hypothesis for Exercise 2.) If A has all coequalizers, G preserves all coequalizers, and G reflects isomorphisms, prove that G reflects all coequalizers.

items.name: canonical presentation of a T-algebra; M as a coequalizer
items.statement_summary: (a) Show the canonical presentation of a T-algebra <x,h> is <T^2 x, mu_{Tx}> => <Tx, mu_x> -> <x,h> (parallel arrows mu_x and Th, coequalized by h). (b) Show the comparison functor M : X^T -> A in Beck's theorem appears as a coequalizer diagram FGFx => Fx -> M(x,h) (parallel arrows eps_{Fx} and Fh).

items.name: left adjoint to K from coequalizers of split-under-G pairs
items.statement_summary: Let P be the set of parallel pairs f,g : a => b in A such that <Gf,Gg> has a split coequalizer. Using Exercise 4(b): (a) if A has coequalizers of all pairs in P, then K has a left adjoint M; (b) if in addition G preserves coequalizers of pairs in P, the unit eta : I -> K.M is an isomorphism; (c) if in addition to (a) G reflects coequalizers of pairs in P, the counit M.K -> I is an isomorphism.

items.name: Beck's theorem up to equivalence
items.statement_summary: Using Exercise 5 and Theorem IV.4.1, prove the equivalence-version of Beck's theorem: given data (1),(2), the following are equivalent -- (i) the comparison K : A -> X^T is an equivalence of categories; (ii) for every parallel pair f,g in A for which <Gf,Gg> has an absolute coequalizer, A has a coequalizer of f,g and G preserves and reflects coequalizers of such pairs; (iii) the same with 'absolute coequalizer' replaced by 'split coequalizer'.

items.name: Crude Tripleability Theorem (Barr-Beck)
items.statement_summary: CTT: if G is CTT then the comparison functor K is an equivalence of categories.

items.name: Vulgar Tripleability Theorem
items.statement_summary: VTT: if G is VTT then the comparison functor K is an equivalence of categories.

items.name: composite CTT/PTT/VTT is PTT
items.statement_summary: Given functors G1 : A -> X, G2 : X -> Y, G3 : Y -> Z with G1 CTT, G2 PTT, G3 VTT, prove that the composite G3.G2.G1 is PTT.

items.name: composite of two VTT is VTT
items.statement_summary: Prove that the composite of two VTT functors is VTT.

items.name: composite of two CTT is CTT
items.statement_summary: Prove that the composite of two CTT functors is CTT.

items.name: algebras of a variety are T-algebras (comparison is an isomorphism)
items.statement_summary: Let Omega be a set of operators, E a set of identities on the derived operators, G the forgetful functor from the category <Omega,E>-Alg of all small <Omega,E>-algebras to Set, and T the induced monad on Set. Then the comparison functor K : <Omega,E>-Alg -> Set^T is an isomorphism. Proof via Beck's theorem: G creates coequalizers of pairs whose underlying maps have an absolute coequalizer e, defining each operation on the codomain via the n-th power e^n (still a coequalizer).

items.name: Theorem 1 via split coequalizers
items.statement_summary: Prove Theorem 1 using split coequalizers instead of absolute coequalizers, defining each operation on the codomain X from a splitting <s,t> of the fork (1) by omega_X(x1,...,xn) = e . omega_B(s x1,...,s xn) for xi in X; for n=2 this is like the usual product of cosets of a normal subgroup.

items.name: Beck's theorem for K-Alg over K-Mod
items.statement_summary: For K a commutative ring, show that Beck's theorem applies to the forgetful functor K-Alg -> K-Mod.

items.name: the forgetful functor Cmpt Haus -> Set is monadic
items.statement_summary: The standard forgetful functor G : Cmpt Haus -> Set, sending each (small) compact Hausdorff space to its underlying set, is monadic. Its left adjoint F assigns to a set X the Stone-Cech compactification (V.6.2) of X with the discrete topology; the proof (due to Pare) shows G creates coequalizers for pairs whose underlying set-maps have an absolute coequalizer, transporting the closure operation along e and checking the quotient is compact Hausdorff.

items.name: topological space as a closure space; continuous and closed maps
items.statement_summary: For the proof a topological space is regarded as a pair (X, closure) with a closure operation S |-> Sbar on subsets satisfying the Kuratowski axioms: emptyset-bar = emptyset, S subset Sbar, Sbar-bar = Sbar, (S union T)-bar = Sbar union Tbar. A continuous map f : (X,cl_X) -> (Y,cl_Y) is a function with f(Sbar) subset f(S)-bar for all S; f is closed if f(Sbar) superset f(S)-bar for all S.

items.name: continuous map from compact to Hausdorff is closed
items.statement_summary: If X is a compact space and Y a Hausdorff space, then every continuous map f : (X,cl_X) -> (Y,cl_Y) is closed.

items.name: the constructed topology on W is the quotient topology
items.statement_summary: Show that the topology on the coequalizer object W built in the proof of Theorem 1 is the quotient topology on W defined by e : Y -> W, i.e. a subset of W is open iff its inverse image under e is open in Y.
